blueprint.summary: Connect uncertainty, binary coding and probabilistic prediction through entropy, cross-entropy and directed KL, with explicit support, units and reference measures.
outcomes: Explain why logarithmic surprise adds across independent outcomes
Compute entropy and distinguish ideal cost from actual prefix-code lengths
Calculate cross-entropy and signed KL contributions with correct zero-support rules
Prove nonnegative KL and diagnose direction and metric mistakes
Use conditional entropy and stable logits to interpret prediction loss
Compare accuracy, held-out log loss and perplexity on a consistent evaluation set
Separate discrete entropy from coordinate-dependent differential entropy
Certify a finite moment-constrained maximum-entropy distribution
sequence: Start with an outcome and its logarithmic surprise
Encode and decode actual prefix words
Charge source outcomes using another model and derive KL
Prove the bounds and explain direction
Compute stable log loss and evaluate comparable predictions
Preserve probability under changes of continuous units
Use KL to certify a moment-constrained maximum
Practise changed assumptions and connect to mutual information

visual.type: Binary address tree, codeword decoder, weighted surprise strips, signed mismatch contributions, conditional probability mosaic, density scaling and a feasible entropy slice
visual.question: Which distribution supplies the outcomes, which supplies their price, and which changes preserve the probability or constraint?
visual.interaction: Change a source/model, decode a message, inspect conditional prediction, change coordinates and move along a mean-preserving probability slice.

practice.task: Calculate changed uncertainty and loss, decode a prefix message, repair a support or unit error and certify a new constrained maximum.
practice.success: Correct inputs and units, justified zero/infinite conventions, independently computed results and explanations that separate mathematical bounds from empirical evaluation.

misconceptions: Entropy is always an attainable one-symbol code length
Every individual KL contribution is nonnegative
Clipping a zero prediction preserves the original score
Marginal label entropy is the ideal loss when features matter
KL is symmetric or obeys a triangle inequality
Differential entropy is a coordinate-invariant number of bits
A continuous model has finite KL from the empirical point-mass distribution
Every exponential tilt maximizes ordinary Shannon entropy
blueprint.reviewFocus: Prefix overhead and source assumptions, signed contributions versus nonnegative totals, support infinities, conditional risk, stable logits, evaluation denominators, reference/coordinate conventions and finite maximum-entropy certificates.
